sections.label: Corporate Income Tax rebate increase
sections.summary: The existing Corporate Income Tax rebate rises from 30% to 50% of tax payable, capped at $20,000 yearly for Years of Assessment 2016 and 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, the existing Corporate Income Tax rebate will be raised from 30% to 50% of tax payable, with a cap of $20,000 rebate each year for Years of Assessment 2016 and 2017.

sections.label: M&A scheme enhancement
sections.summary: The M&A scheme was enhanced to allow 25% tax allowance on the first $40 million of qualifying share acquisition costs each year, up from $20 million.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Second, to support more mergers and acquisitions, the M&A scheme was enhanced to allow 25% tax allowance on the first $40 million of the cost of qualifying share acquisitions incurred each year, up from $20 million.

sections.label: Personal income tax relief cap
sections.summary: The total personal income tax reliefs an individual can claim will be capped at $80,000 per Year of Assessment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Fifth, to enhance progressivity of our personal income tax systems, the total amount of personal income tax reliefs an individual can claim will be capped at $80,000 per Year of Assessment.

sections.label: Questions on CIT rebate cap
sections.summary: The Bill raises the rebate rate for Years of Assessment 2016 to 2017 from 30% to 50% but retains the $20,000 cap, prompting questions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The current Bill seeks to increase the rebate rate for Years of Assessment 2016 to 2017 from 30% to 50%, but retains the cap at $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify the rationale behind reducing the cap by $10,000?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And in view of the sluggish economy ahead, will the Senior Minister of State also consider not just increasing the rebate rate but also increasing the cap?

sections.label: Budget 2013 CIT rebate
sections.summary: Budget 2013 gave a three-year CIT rebate of 30% of tax payable, capped at $30,000 per Year of Assessment from YA 2013 to YA 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In Budget 2013, a three-year CIT rebate of 30% of tax payable, capped at $30,000 per Year of Assessment (YA) from YA 2013 to YA 2015 was given as part of the three-year transition support package to support firms in their restructuring efforts.

sections.label: Budget 2016 CIT rebate enhancement
sections.summary: Amid difficult business conditions, the CIT rebate was enhanced in Budget 2016 from 30% to 50% of tax payable, keeping the $20,000 cap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In light of the difficult and uncertain business conditions amidst the economic slowdown, the CIT rebate was further enhanced in Budget 2016 from 30% of tax payable to 50% of tax payable, but the cap of $20,000 rebate for each year for YA 2016 to 2017 was maintained.

sections.label: Corporate income tax e-filing requirements
sections.summary: Companies with turnover over $10 million in YA 2017 must e-file for YA 2018, over $1 million in YA 2018 for YA 2019, and all other small companies from YA 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, companies with turnover of more than $10 million in YA 2017 will be required to e-file for YA 2018; Second, companies with turnover of more than $1 million in YA 2018 will be required to e-file for YA 2019; Third, all other small companies will only be required to e-file their corporate income tax returns from YA 2020.
